# firstboot_volume (Resource)

A block storage volume.

Billed per GB-hour at its PROVISIONED size from creation to deletion, whether or not it is attached. A detached volume still costs money.

**Volumes are excluded from server backups.** Whatever lives here needs its own backup arrangement.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The volume's name. The API has no rename, so changing it replaces the volume, which DESTROYS its data.
- `size_gb` (Number) Size in GB. **Grow only.** A smaller value is refused by the API at apply time rather than at plan time, and growing charges the difference. Read `firstboot_volume_limits` rather than assuming a band: the minimum and maximum are operator policy with per-account overrides.

### Optional

- `automount` (Boolean) Whether the volume is mounted inside the guest on attach, via an fstab line keyed by UUID and carrying `nofail`.

Defaults to `false` for a reason: a running server's fstab was written by its owner, and mounting over it on the next attach is a surprise rather than a convenience.
- `fs_type` (String) Filesystem to create at BIRTH, e.g. `ext4` or `xfs`. Omit for a raw block device.

**Accepted only at creation and never again.** A volume is formatted once, when the disk is provably empty; afterwards nothing can honestly answer "does this hold data", so nothing is allowed to try. Changing it replaces the volume and destroys what is on it.
- `project_id` (String) Optional project to group the volume under. Changing it moves the volume in place; it is not a replacement.
- `server_id` (String) Server to attach to. Changing this detaches from one server and attaches to the other, in place; it does not replace the volume. At most five volumes per server.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags on this volume, used to select it from a `firstboot_*` data source and to filter it in the panel.

At most 10, each up to 32 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `:` and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit. `env:prod` is a convention, not a schema: a tag is one flat string.

**Written exactly as given.** The API stores tags lowercased, so a tag that is not already lowercase is refused at plan time rather than silently rewritten — a rewritten value would differ from the configuration on every subsequent plan.
- `wait_for_ready` (Boolean) Whether apply waits for the volume to finish provisioning.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `mount_path` (String)
- `mount_state` (String) Whether the in-guest mount succeeded. A failure here does NOT fail the attachment: the disk really is attached and the manual instructions still work.
- `state` (String) `available` or `attached` are settled; `error` is a failure.
